title: Should we move from our Bangi house to a new Cyberjaya condo to cut the commute?
videoTitle: ASKING SEAN #220 | MAKE DECISIONS BASED ON MARKET DATA
excerpt: Two civil servants want to swap their Bangi terrace for a RM575,000 Cyberjaya condo to shorten the school run. Sean says high-rise prices there have fallen, so compare 20 projects, or simply rent.

qa.asker: E, a viewer who wrote in by email
qa.context: E, 40, and her husband are civil servants who have lived in a Bangi terrace house since 2014, now valued at about RM430,000 to RM530,000. Their son's playschool is in Cyberjaya and E works in Putrajaya, a journey of about 90 minutes. They are looking at a Cyberjaya condo due in 2025, with a loan of about RM575,000 over 29 years and about RM3,200 a month including maintenance, though E retires in 19 years.
qa.question: Should they rent out or sell the Bangi house, is RM3,200 a month a burden, and what are Cyberjaya's prospects if they sell in 20 years?
qa.quote: We rent things that depreciates in value.
qa.answer: First check the numbers they left out: their joint income and how much is still owed on the Bangi house. Cyberjaya high-rises have generally lost value, so before committing RM3,200 a month for 29 years, compare about 20 projects nearby, consider Putrajaya, or simply rent in Cyberjaya, which is cheap for the space you get.

reasons.title: Selling may free less than you think
reasons.body: In the first years of a loan most of each instalment goes to interest, so a house bought around RM400,000 may still owe about RM380,000 after ten years. After any RPGT on the gain, the cash arrives six to eight months after the sale.

reasons.title: Cyberjaya high-rises have struggled
reasons.body: The town has jobs and amenities, but rental demand hasn't followed, and many condos end up at auction. A friend of Sean's bought at RM450,000 ten years ago; similar units now go for about RM280,000.

reasons.title: Rent what loses value
reasons.body: Where high-rise prices are falling, rents are low too, so a bigger unit or even a landed home can be rented for less than the RM3,200 instalment. Distances in Cyberjaya are also quick to drive, so living right beside the school isn't essential.

reasons.title: Sales galleries are built to close
reasons.body: Sean once designed sales galleries and says most buyers who walk in end up booking. Comparing other projects, and Putrajaya, which has performed better, protects against an emotional purchase.

actions: Work out your joint income and check the instalment is no more than about a third of it.
Find out how much you still owe on the Bangi house and what it would sell for after costs.
Visit about 20 projects around Cyberjaya and Putrajaya, including subsales, before booking.
Price what RM2,500 to RM2,600 a month would rent in Cyberjaya, and compare it with buying.
If you keep the Bangi house to rent out, don't expect a landed home's rent to cover a loan.
qa.caveat: If one specific school is non-negotiable, living nearby matters more. Sean notes Cyberjaya's landed homes have done well; his concern is its high-rise market.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #220. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in August 2023. Sean says he used to design property sales galleries.
